text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors) THE AUSTRALIAN

FINANCIAL REVIEW The Energy Users Group has queried whether plans unveiled in last week's New South Wales Budget to impose a A$100 million levy is in breach of national competition principles, and has lodged a complaint with the National Competition Council. The Group sas it will raise its concerns directly with the State's Treasurer and Energy Minister Michael Egan. Page 5. -- Federal Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith has told Channel Ten's Meet the Press program that the Government would give "serious consideration" to a plan to introduce new legislation creating a blanket exemption from unfair dismissal laws for every Australian business, after a similar plan was last week defeated in the Senate. Page 5. -- Retail shareholders of Colonial Ltd are promised substantial stag profits after the price for institutional investors was set yesterday at 50 cents above the retail price. Colonial will have the largest share register in Australia with 534,000 shareholders, and only 23 per cent of existing holders electing to sell their entitlements into the public offer. Page 21. -- New Zealand's Brierley Investments Ltd will announce details today of a A$388 million float of Weeks Bass Strait Royalty, which will realise a book profit of A$87.5 million. It is believed Brierley's Australian oil asset will be floated in the form of a trust, providing institutional and retail investors with tax advantages. Page 21. -- Automotive Components Ltd has upped the stakes in the A$500 million automotive spare parts market after paying an estimated A$20 million for Federal-Mogul's chain of 13 retail and wholesale outlets, and is now focused on competing with rivals Atkins Carlyle, Coventry Group and Pacific Dunlop. Page 23 -- An earnings slump to the order of 15 per cent in the McPherson's Ltd housewares and printing group has been blamed on poor performances from its United States market. Directors of the company have already signalled they intend to make a series of managemnt changes and a reorganisation of the US operation. Page 23. --

THE AUSTRALIAN Colonial Ltd is expected to give shareholders an initial windfall of A$265 million when the group lists today at an expected hefty premium to the confirmed issue price of A$2.60 a share. Colonial managing director Peter Smedley expects the shares to make a strong debut, but many investors are disappointed Colonial savagely cut back on public applications to only 350 shares and attached options. Page 29. -- Prime Minister John Howard has accused the Business Council of Australia of wanting a sustained Budget surplus, but also demanding business relief measures costing up to A$5 billion. Howard also said the Council's criticism of the Federal Government's buiness policies was "puzzling" because the Government had delivered on much of what the BCA had requested. Page 29. -- A report commissioned by West Australian woodchip company Bunnings Forest Products says Japanese pulp and paper manufacturers are unlikely to keep using woodchips from the State's native forests because of better, cheaper eucalyptus now available on the mrket from plantations in other countries. Page 29. -- Telstra Corp and its State-owned operations have held a monopoly on the Australian telecommunications market for 90 years, but this will be under scrutiny when the industry becomes fully deregulated on July 1. All players in the sector are aware that thesuccess of market deregulation in bringing about effective competition will rely on Telstra's desire to negotiate fairly on key issues. Page 29. -- According to Linda Nichols, who was a member of the Wallis inquiry investigation of the financial system, the superannuation funds management industry may be reduced to as few as 30 institution following the competition measures announced in the Federal Bdget. Nichols says the key recommendations have been taken on board by Treasurer Peter Costello and the superannuation industry is facing a major rationalisation. Page 31. -- National Australia Bank managing director Don Argus said yesterday all of the main Australian banks are being considered by foreign banks as takeover targets. Argus said he was scared the National Australia Bank was being sought by unnamed foreign banks n the wake of Federal Treasurer Peter Costello's statement last month that a purchase of a major bank by a foreign investor could be acceptable. Page 32. -- THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD Colonial Group's listing on the Australian Stock Exchange today will result in the largest number of shareholders of any Australian company expected to reap the rewards of a huge initial profit. A profit of at least 50 cents a share is expected on the prce paid by the public, with the group having 533,803 shareholders. Page 33. -- In a move expected to be the first by the four major banks, the ANZ Banking Group will shake up the private health insurance industry by launching its own private health insurance product later this month. The product will be sold through the ANZ's bank banch network by National Mutual. Page 33. -- WMC has joined the growing list of companies to decrease its Australian exploration expenditure in favour of several overseas prospects. A company spokesman confirmed the amount spent on Australian exploration would "reduce substantially" with much of th money to spent overseas, particularly in Canada, South America and the Philippines. Page 35. -- Recent cold weather is providing a boost for retailers, with major stores reporting a strong gain in sales during the last week. Chain department stores Myer Grace Brothers and David Jones said last week, which included Mother's Day, was the best day's trading of at least the last four years. Page 35. -- Lower interest rates are continuing to drive house prices higher in Sydney and other capital cities, although increases in some cities are marginal amid continuing concern over the economy. Real Estate Institute of Australia president Don Brindley says dspite lower mortgage rates, the real estate market rises in the residential property market are being diminished by generally high levels of unemployment and low consumer confidence. -- Investors have been surprised recently by the rises in ICI Australia's stock prices. There have been queries as to the cause of the rise, with ICI's parent about to sell its A$2 billion-plus holding in the Australian division. Analysts are not surprised and believe ICI Australia to be under-valued and trading at a discount compared with other cyclical stocks. Page 36. -- THE AGE Colonial Ltd managing director Peter Smedley has expressed optimism over his company's profit potential, announcing yesterday it would have 533,803 on its shareholder listing, topping the 520,000 held by National Mutual and 370,000 by the Commonwealth Ban. Smedley felt the company's share price would list at around A$3.10, meaning its market capitalisation would be close to A$1.8 billion. Page B1. -- The Australian Stock Exchange has warned that a plan unveiled in last week's Federal Budget to ban trading in franking credits on share dividends has already adversely affected trading, and could have a further negative impact on derivatives trading, the fastest growing area in the financial markets. Page B1. -- Cue Energy Resources NL has struck a lucrative deal with Saga Petroleum to acquire oil and gas interests on the Jambi Merang block in Indonesia. The A$34.7 million deal gives Cue an estimated 133 billion cubic feet of gas and 5.3 million barrels of light oil. Page B3. -- The Infrastructure and Investment Corporation, which represents a number of high-profile investors and is backed by many of the country's largest business groups, is expected to sell its 70 per cent stake in the Port of Geelong, only a year after the Victorian Government sold it for A$50.5 million. -- The Australian mining industry's gamble on the fluctuating copper market appears to have paid off, after remarkable growth in consumption levels at twice the rate of western GDP's growth, and the continued decline in copper stocks have combined to increas the mineral's price recovery to US$1.16 a pound. Page B3. -- Speaking on channel Nine's Sunday program, British publishing company Pearson Group plc has revealed it has set its sights on the lucrative Fairfax stable of newspapers, which is expected to be up for grabs following an anticipated change to the country'scross media ownership laws.
